mainTopic: Which consecrated birds are exempt from שילוח הקן, and responsibility for lost הקדש ('in God's treasury', עלי vs. הרי זו)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a point about a bird sentenced by a court: it must be a case where the verdict was not yet given, so it still has to be brought to בית דין. Then the גמרא asks what case the משנה means when it exempts מוקדשין from שילוח הקן. Four suggestions fail: a nest at home is never included, you cannot consecrate a nest you do not own, chicks taken and returned are exempt anyway, and a mother bird's duty of שילוח began before she was consecrated. רב says the case is altar-consecrated dovecote birds that fled. שמואל says it is a chicken consecrated for בדק הבית that ran away, because 'wherever it is, it is in God's treasury.' רבי יוחנן agrees with שמואל, and ריש לקיש objects. The גמרא then raises a contradiction from a case of lost בדק הבית money and resolves each sage's view: ריש לקיש changed his mind, and רבי יוחנן distinguishes 'עלי' from 'הרי זו'. ריש לקיש's position is defended against a ברייתא and a משנה. Finally רב המנונא says everyone agrees there is no responsibility in ערכין, and רבא begins challenging him. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The bird is already sentenced to death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge: if the court already gave its ruling, this bird is meant to be killed, so how could it be sitting freely on its nest?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a bird that is liable to be killed!
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a challenge. The גמרא points out that if the bird's case was already decided, it is a בר קטלא, a creature sentenced to death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird that the court already sentenced should have been killed already. So it does not make sense to picture it resting on its eggs, waiting for someone to send it away. This pushes the גמרא to find a different way to read the case.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable to be killed; under a death sentence

phrases.english: It is subject to being killed,
phrases.notes: This is the end of a question that began before this section: if the verdict was already given, the bird should already be dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a challenge that started in the text just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the bird under discussion already had its verdict given.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bird already sentenced to death should have been killed, so it could not be sitting on its nest.

steps.title: The court has not yet ruled on the bird
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the court has not yet given its ruling. There is still a duty to bring the bird to court and fulfill ובערת הרע מקרבך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a case where its verdict was not yet given, and one needs to bring it to the court and fulfill through it the פסוק: 'And you shall remove the evil from your midst.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The case is a bird whose final verdict has not yet been issued (לא גמר דיניה), so it is still alive, but someone needs to bring it to בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the verdict was not given, the bird is not yet 'sentenced,' so it can be resting on its nest. Still, there is a duty to bring it to court, based on ובערת הרע מקרבך. That duty is why this bird is treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: The final verdict of a court
A Jewish court
'And you shall remove the evil from your midst', the duty to remove wrongdoing through the court

phrases.english: Rather, it is where its verdict was not yet issued,
and one needs to bring it to the court
and fulfill through it: "And you shall remove the evil from your midst."
phrases.notes: דברים 13:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by changing the case to one before the verdict.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the bird had already been sentenced, so it should already be dead.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verdict has not been given yet. The bird is alive, but it must be brought to court to fulfill ובערת הרע מקרבך.

steps.title: What case of consecrated birds does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: the גמרא asks what exact situation the משנה has in mind when it exempts מוקדשין from שילוח הקן.
steps.simpleTranslation: These consecrated birds, what is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the משנה's rule that consecrated birds are exempt from sending away the mother. It is setting up a search for the right case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is hard to picture how a wild bird's nest could become consecrated in the first place. The גמרא will now test possible cases one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrated items that belong to the בית המקדש
What is the case? What situation are we talking about?
The מצוה to send away the mother bird before taking the young

phrases.english: These consecrated birds, what are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact case in which a bird's nest is consecrated, so that the משנה's exemption applies.

steps.title: First try: he consecrated a nest in his own house
steps.stepSummary: First suggestion: a person had a nest in his house and consecrated it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say he had a nest inside his house and consecrated it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible case. Since the nest is in his house, it is his, so he can consecrate it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This solves the ownership problem, because you can consecrate what is yours. The next step will test whether שילוח הקן would even apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a suggestion that will be tested
He consecrated it

phrases.english: If we say that he had a nest
inside his house, and he consecrated it –

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ קֵן בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First proposed answer to the question in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A nest he owned in his house that he consecrated.

steps.title: A nest at home is never included in the מצוה
steps.stepSummary: Rejected: the פסוק says 'if a bird's nest happens before you,' which leaves out a nest that is already at hand (מזומן). So even an unconsecrated nest at home has no מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is one obligated in such a case? 'If a bird's nest happens before you' excludes one that is readily available.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first case. A nest in your house is never included in שילוח הקן, so the משנה would not need to exempt it because it is consecrated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words כי יקרא mean the nest just happens to come across your path. A nest in your own house is מזומן, already at hand, so it is exempt even when it is not consecrated. That means this cannot be the case the משנה is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If it happens before you', by chance
Excluding what is already at hand, a nest that is already yours
Is he obligated? A question that really means 'no'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this means consecrated birds are fine to take. The point is only that this case cannot be what the משנה means, because a home nest is exempt anyway.

phrases.english: Is one obligated?
"If a bird's nest happens before you" –
phrases.notes: דברים 22:6

phrases.english: excluding one that is readily available.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי מִיחַיַּיב? כִּי יִקָּרֵא קַן צִפּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the case suggested in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of a nest in his own house.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A nest at home is מזומן and is excluded from the מצוה even without being consecrated, so the משנה's exemption would teach nothing.

steps.title: Second try: he consecrated a nest he saw outside
steps.stepSummary: Second suggestion: he saw a nest out in the open and consecrated it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he saw a nest out in the world and consecrated it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second case. This nest is not at home, so it does fall under כי יקרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gets around the problem of מזומן. Now the question is whether he can consecrate a nest that is not his.

keyTerms.meaning: Out in the world; somewhere ordinary, not in his property

phrases.english: Rather, where he saw a nest out in the open and consecrated it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected case with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A nest he found outside and consecrated.

steps.title: You cannot consecrate what you do not own
steps.stepSummary: Rejected: the פסוק about consecrating 'his house' teaches that you can only consecrate what is in your possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is it consecrated? The Torah says 'When a man consecrates his house as holy': just as his house is his, so too anything consecrated must be his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second case. A nest out in the open is not his, so his consecrating it does nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From 'his house' we learn that הקדש works only on something in your possession (ברשותו). A wild nest is not yours, so it never becomes מוקדשין, and the case fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy, consecrated
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah
In his possession

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule of הקדש: a person cannot consecrate something that is not his.

phrases.english: But is it consecrated?

phrases.aramaic: ״אִישׁ כִּי יַקְדִּשׁ אֶת בֵּיתוֹ קֹדֶשׁ״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא,
phrases.english: The Torah says: "When a man consecrates his house as holy,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:14

phrases.english: just as his house is in his possession,
so too anything he consecrates must be in his possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the case suggested in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of consecrating a nest found outside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק teaches that only things in your possession can be consecrated, and an ownerless nest is not yours.

steps.title: Third try: he picked up the chicks, consecrated them, and put them back
steps.stepSummary: Third suggestion: he lifted the chicks, which makes them his, consecrated them, and then returned them to the nest.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he lifted up the chicks, consecrated them, and then put them back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third case that solves the ownership problem. Lifting the chicks makes them his, so he can consecrate them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting (הגבהה) is a way of acquiring something, so the chicks are now his and the הקדש works. After that he returns them to the nest. The next step checks whether שילוח הקן would apply at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He lifted them up, which is a way of acquiring
Chicks
He returned them

phrases.english: Rather, where he lifted up the chicks,
phrases.notes: By lifting them he takes them for himself, so now they are his and he can consecrate them.

phrases.english: and consecrated them, and then returned them –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected case with a third one that solves the ownership problem.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He acquired the chicks by lifting them, consecrated them, and returned them to the nest.

steps.title: Chicks that were taken and put back are exempt anyway
steps.stepSummary: Rejected: a משנה teaches that if someone took the young and returned them, and the mother came back, there is no duty to send her away, even with unconsecrated birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: In this case, even with ordinary birds he is not obligated, as it was taught: if he took the young and returned them to the nest, and afterward the mother came back to them, he is exempt from sending her away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the third case as well. Once he took the chicks and put them back, there is no מצוה even with חולין, so the משנה's exemption for מוקדשין would teach nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After he picks up the chicks they are his, already at hand, so they no longer count as a nest that 'happens before you.' Since even ordinary birds are exempt here, this case cannot explain why the משנה singles out consecrated birds. The search for the right case continues.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, unconsecrated things
Exempt from sending away the mother
Also, too

steps.whatToRemember: All three cases fail. A nest at home is never included, a nest you do not own cannot be consecrated, and chicks taken and returned are exempt anyway. The גמרא still needs a case where consecrated birds are exempt only because they are consecrated.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי אֲפִילּוּ בְּחוּלִּין נָמֵי לָא מִיחַיַּיב,
phrases.english: In this case, even with ordinary birds he is also not obligated,
as it was taught: If he took the young
and returned them to the nest,
and afterward the mother came back onto them –
he is exempt from sending her away.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי אֲפִילּוּ בְּחוּלִּין נָמֵי לָא מִיחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the case suggested in step 8 using a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of chicks that were lifted, consecrated, and returned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה rules that chicks taken and returned are exempt even when they are not consecrated, so the משנה's special exemption for מוקדשין would be pointless.

steps.title: Fourth suggestion: he lifted the mother, consecrated her, and put her back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה means a case where someone lifted the mother bird, consecrated her, and returned her to the nest.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where he lifted the mother, consecrated her, and put her back.
steps.whatsHappening: After the chicks idea was rejected, the גמרא now tries the same trick with the mother bird instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting the mother makes her his, so he can consecrate her, which answers the problem from step 7. Putting her back is meant to create a nest that has a consecrated mother sitting on it.

keyTerms.meaning: He lifted her, which is a way of acquiring something
The mother bird
He returned her to the nest

phrases.english: Rather, where he lifted the mother,
phrases.notes: Lifting the bird makes it his, so now he is able to consecrate it.

phrases.english: and consecrated her, and returned her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected chicks case from step 8 with a case about the mother.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is where the mother was lifted, consecrated, and put back on the nest.

steps.title: The duty to send her away began before she was consecrated
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected: when he first found the mother on the nest, he was already obligated to send her away, before he consecrated her.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the start he was obligated to send her away, before he consecrated her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the fourth suggestion. The duty of שילוח started the moment he found her, and consecrating her later can't erase it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the moment he came across the nest, the mother was an ordinary bird, so the מצוה of שילוח applied. Making her הקדש afterward does not cancel a duty that already took hold. So this is not a case where הקדש exempts.

keyTerms.meaning: From the beginning, at first
He became obligated
Sending away the mother bird

phrases.english: From the start he became obligated in sending away
before he consecrated her,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the case suggested in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of lifting, consecrating, and returning the mother.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the duty of שילוח has started, consecrating the bird later cannot remove it.

steps.title: Proof from covering the blood: a duty that already began stays
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יוחנן בן יוסף shows that if a duty began before הקדש, consecrating afterward does not cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוחנן בן יוסף says, if he consecrated a wild animal and then slaughtered it, he does not need to cover the blood. If he slaughtered it and then consecrated it, he must cover the blood, since he was already obligated to cover before it became הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the rule it just used. It comes from the מצוה of covering the blood, כיסוי הדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Consecrated animals are exempt from כיסוי הדם. But order matters: if slaughter came first, the duty already took hold and later הקדש cannot remove it. The same idea applies to the mother bird in step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: A wild animal, whose blood must be covered after slaughter
Covering the blood after slaughter (כיסוי הדם)
Something consecrated, belonging to the Temple

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a general rule: a duty that has already started is not cancelled when the object later becomes הקדש.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן יוֹסֵף אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Yosef says:
If he consecrated a wild animal and then slaughtered it,
he is exempt from covering,
phrases.notes: He means covering the blood. Consecrated animals don't have this מצוה.

phrases.english: if he slaughtered it and then consecrated it,
he is obligated to cover,
since he was already obligated in covering
before it came into the status of consecrated property.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן יוֹסֵף אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rejection in step 11 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a duty which began before הקדש is not cancelled by later הקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יוחנן בן יוסף about covering the blood.

steps.title: רב: consecrated dovecote chicks that flew away
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה means chicks from his dovecote that he consecrated, which later fled and made a nest elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: it is where he consecrated the young of his dovecote, and they rebelled and flew off.
steps.whatsHappening: After all the suggestions failed, רב gives a fresh case for the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The birds were consecrated while still his, at home, so the consecration works. Then they fled and nested out in the open, so the nest really does 'happen before you.' They are exempt from שילוח because they are holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'fruits of his dovecote,' meaning the young birds born there
They rebelled, meaning they flew away and nested elsewhere

phrases.english: Rav says: it is about one who consecrates the young of his dovecote
phrases.notes: He consecrated them as offerings for the altar.

phrases.english: and they rebelled,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: בְּמַקְדִּישׁ פֵּירוֹת שׁוֹבָכוֹ וּמָרְדוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new answer after all the earlier suggestions were rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dovecote chicks consecrated for the altar that later fled and nested elsewhere.

steps.title: שמואל: a chicken consecrated for Temple upkeep
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the משנה means a chicken consecrated for בדק הבית, the upkeep of the Temple building, which later ran away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל says: it is where he consecrated his chicken for Temple upkeep.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different case for the משנה, using a chicken given to the Temple building fund.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The setup is like רב's case: consecrated at home, then it ran off and nested elsewhere. The difference is the type of holiness. This chicken is not an offering; it is donated for its money value.

keyTerms.meaning: His chicken
Upkeep of the Temple building, a fund that uses things for their value

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
it is about one who consecrates his chicken for Temple upkeep.
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes, as in רב's case, that the chicken then ran away and nested elsewhere.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: בְּמַקְדִּישׁ תַּרְנְגוֹלְתּוֹ לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different case alongside רב's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A chicken consecrated for בדק הבית that later fled.

steps.title: Why did רב not accept שמואל's case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why שמואל didn't limit himself to רב's case, but asks why רב didn't give שמואל's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that שמואל did not say like רב, because he applies the משנה even to things consecrated for Temple upkeep. But why did רב not say like שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב chose a narrower case. This question sets up the next step, where רב's reason is explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's case is wider: if even Temple-upkeep birds are exempt, altar birds surely are. So שמואל has nothing to gain from רב's case. But רב's silence about the Temple-upkeep chicken needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that..., introducing what is understood before asking the hard part
He sets the case as, he explains it as being about
Things consecrated for Temple upkeep

phrases.english: It makes sense that Shmuel did not say like Rav,

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָא מוֹקֵים לַהּ בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: since he explains it as being about items consecrated for Temple upkeep,
phrases.notes: שמואל holds even this lighter holiness exempts, so altar birds certainly do.

phrases.english: but Rav, what is the reason
he did not say like Shmuel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers from steps 13 and 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב limited the משנה to altar-consecrated birds and did not include Temple-upkeep birds.

steps.title: רב: altar holiness stays, value holiness falls away
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that birds consecrated for the altar keep their holiness even after fleeing, but a chicken consecrated for Temple upkeep loses its holiness when it runs away, so it must be sent away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב would tell you: I exempted from שילוח only things like the young of his dovecote, which are consecrated for the altar. Since they have holiness of the body itself, their holiness doesn't leave them. But one who consecrates his chicken for Temple upkeep, which is not for the altar and has only value-holiness, once it runs off its holiness falls away, and it must be sent away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 15. רב thinks the two kinds of holiness act differently when the bird flees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קדושת הגוף, holiness of the body itself, sticks to the bird even when it flies off. קדושת דמים, holiness only for its money value, falls away once the bird escapes. So in שמואל's case the chicken is ordinary again and the מצוה of שילוח applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Things consecrated as offerings for the altar
Holiness of the body itself, which stays on the object
Holiness only for the object's money value
It fell away, it ended

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב: a bird consecrated for the altar stays holy even after it flees, so it is exempt from שילוח. A bird consecrated for Temple upkeep loses its holiness once it flees, so it must be sent away.
steps.confusionAlert: רב does not say Temple-upkeep birds were never holy. They were holy, but that lighter holiness falls away once the bird runs off.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the two kinds of הקדש can lead to different halachic results when the object leaves its owner.

phrases.english: Rav would say to you:
I specifically exempted from sending away
in a case such as the young of his dovecote,
which are consecrated for the altar,
since they are consecrated with holiness of the body itself,
their holiness does not fall away from them,
but one who consecrates his chicken for Temple upkeep,
which is not consecrated for the altar,
but merely has holiness of value,
phrases.notes: The chicken is not offered. It is holy only because its value belongs to the Temple.

phrases.english: once it ran off, its holiness falls away,
and it is subject to sending away.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב: דַּוְקָא קָפָטְרִי מִשִּׁילּוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Altar holiness (קדושת הגוף) stays after the bird flees; value holiness (קדושת דמים) falls away, so that bird must be sent away.

steps.title: שמואל's reason: the chicken is still in God's treasury
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds that a chicken consecrated for בדק הבית keeps its holiness even after it runs away, because wherever it is, it belongs to ה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל says: wherever it is, it is in the treasury of the Merciful One, as the פסוק says, 'The earth is the Lord's and all that fills it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל was willing to set the משנה in the case of a chicken consecrated for בדק הבית. He holds that its holiness does not go away when it runs off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 16 we learned that רב holds a runaway בדק הבית chicken loses its holiness. שמואל disagrees: since the whole world belongs to ה', the chicken never really left הקדש's possession. That is why it stays holy, and so it is exempt from שילוח הקן, just as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: The treasury of the Merciful One, meaning God's storehouse
Wherever it is
The earth and all that fills it belong to ה'

steps.whyThisMatters: This phrase, 'wherever it is, it is in God's treasury,' is the key idea for the rest of this section.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
wherever it is,
it is in the treasury of the Merciful One,
as it is written: "The earth is the Lord's, and all that fills it."
phrases.notes: תהלים 24:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives שמואל's side, against רב's view from Step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל holds that a runaway בדק הבית chicken stays holy, since everything is in God's treasury

steps.title: רבי יוחנן agrees with שמואל's case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן also explains the משנה as talking about a chicken consecrated for בדק הבית that ran away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said רבי יוחנן: the משנה is talking about someone who consecrated his chicken for בדק הבית, and it ran away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן, who explains the משנה the same way שמואל does. This sets up an argument with ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן places the משנה in the very case where רב said the holiness is lost. So רבי יוחנן must hold, like שמואל, that the chicken stays holy.

keyTerms.meaning: One who consecrates something to הקדש
Upkeep and repair of the Temple building
It rebelled, meaning it ran away and went wild

phrases.english: And so said Rabbi Yochanan:
it is about one who consecrates his chicken for Temple upkeep
and it ran away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second אמורא who agrees with שמואל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה is about a chicken consecrated for בדק הבית that ran away

steps.title: ריש לקיש objects that its holiness is gone
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן: once the chicken has run away, hasn't its holiness lapsed?
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: but once it ran away, its holiness has lapsed!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן's case. He argues that a runaway chicken is no longer holy, so the משנה could not be talking about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש holds the same view as רב: when a בדק הבית chicken runs away, its holiness lapses. If so, it is now an ordinary bird, so the מצוה of שילוח הקן does apply to it. That means the משנה's exemption for מוקדשין cannot be talking about this case.

keyTerms.meaning: Its holiness has lapsed, meaning it is no longer holy

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said to him:
But once it ran away,
its holiness has lapsed!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁמָּרְדָה פְּקַעָה לַיהּ קְדוּשְׁתַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's case
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's explanation of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A runaway בדק הבית chicken loses its holiness and becomes ordinary, so it would be subject to שילוח. The משנה's exemption therefore cannot be about it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן answers: it is still in God's treasury
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the chicken stays holy, because wherever it is, it is in God's treasury.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: it is in the treasury of the Merciful One, as the פסוק says, 'The earth is the Lord's and all that fills it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends himself with the same reason שמואל gave. Running away does not take the chicken out of הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the whole world belongs to ה', a runaway chicken is still 'in' God's treasury. So it never left הקדש's hands, and its holiness stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: It is there (talking about the chicken)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּבֵי גַזָּא דְּרַחֲמָנָא אִיתַאּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: It is in the treasury of the Merciful One,
as it is written: "The earth is the Lord's, and all that fills it."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּבֵי גַזָּא דְּרַחֲמָנָא אִיתַאּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a principle for why the holiness stays
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Running away takes the chicken out of הקדש's possession, so its holiness lapses
steps.terutzMaskana: Everything is in God's treasury, so the chicken stays holy wherever it goes
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן (like שמואל) says a runaway הקדש chicken stays holy. ריש לקיש (like רב) says its holiness lapses.

steps.title: Each sage seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש seem to contradict their own statements made elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא points out a contradiction between רבי יוחנן and רבי יוחנן, and between ריש לקיש and ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא announces a contradiction and will show the other source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that each sage, in a different case, seems to take the opposite position from the one he just took here. The details come next.

keyTerms.meaning: And he threw (one against the other), meaning he pointed out a contradiction

phrases.english: And he pointed out a contradiction between Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yochanan,

phrases.aramaic: וּרְמִי דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אַדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ.
phrases.english: and he pointed out a contradiction between Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against what both sages just said
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש in Steps 18 to 20
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each one seems to hold the opposite view in another case

steps.title: The case of consecrated money that was stolen or lost
steps.stepSummary: About money set aside for בדק הבית that was lost, רבי יוחנן says the owner is still responsible, while ריש לקיש uses 'God's treasury' to say he is not, which is the reverse of their positions above.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: 'This מנה (100 coins) is for בדק הבית,' and the coins were stolen or lost. רבי יוחנן says he is responsible for them until they reach the גזבר. ריש לקיש says: wherever it is, it is in God's treasury, as the פסוק says, 'The earth is the Lord's.' So ריש לקיש contradicts ריש לקיש, and רבי יוחנן contradicts רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the other source, about consecrated money that went missing. Here the two sages seem to have switched sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the chicken case רבי יוחנן said 'it is in God's treasury,' but with the money he says it is not counted as reaching הקדש until the treasurer actually has it. ריש לקיש said the runaway chicken's holiness lapsed, yet with the money he uses the 'God's treasury' idea himself. Each one seems to argue against his own view.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of 100 זוז
He is responsible for them, meaning he must replace them if lost
The Temple treasurer
A difficulty, a problem in the logic

steps.confusionAlert: Watch closely: the two sages seem to have swapped sides. Here ריש לקיש is the one who says 'it is in God's treasury,' and רבי יוחנן says the owner is still responsible.

phrases.english: As it was stated: "This מנה is for Temple upkeep,"
and they were stolen or lost:
Rabbi Yochanan says: He is responsible for them
until they come into the hands of the treasurer.
And Reish Lakish says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאִיתֵיהּ בְּבֵי גַזָּא דְּרַחֲמָנָא אִיתֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Wherever it is, it is in the treasury of the Merciful One,
phrases.notes: So he holds the owner does not have to replace the lost money.

phrases.english: as it is written: "The earth is the Lord's, and all that fills it."
So Reish Lakish contradicts Reish Lakish,
and Rabbi Yochanan contradicts Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the contradiction announced in Step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the money case each sage takes the opposite of his view in the chicken case

steps.title: ריש לקיש changed his mind after hearing his teacher
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש's contradiction is solved: he said the chicken's holiness lapses before he heard 'God's treasury' from רבי יוחנן, and he ruled on the money case after he heard it.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש's contradiction is not a problem. This statement was made before he heard it from רבי יוחנן his teacher, and that statement was made after he heard it from רבי יוחנן his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves only ריש לקיש's side of the contradiction. It explains that his two statements come from different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His objection that the chicken's holiness lapses came first, before he learned the 'God's treasury' idea. Once רבי יוחנן taught it to him, he accepted it and used it in the money case. רבי יוחנן's own contradiction is handled in steps 24 and 25.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a problem
Before / after
His teacher

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's two views are not a real contradiction. He changed his mind after learning 'God's treasury' from his teacher, רבי יוחנן.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אַדְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לָא קַשְׁיָא,
phrases.english: Reish Lakish against Reish Lakish is not a problem:
this one was before he heard it
phrases.notes: "This one" is his objection about the runaway chicken in Step 19.

phrases.english: from Rabbi Yochanan, his teacher,
and that one was after he heard it
from Rabbi Yochanan, his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אַדְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers half of the contradiction raised in Steps 21 and 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different times: he changed his mind
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש holds two opposite views at once
steps.terutzMaskana: His first view came before he learned from רבי יוחנן, and his later view came after

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן still contradicts himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that even after ריש לקיש's contradiction was solved, רבי יוחנן's two statements still clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, רבי יוחנן's statement contradicts רבי יוחנן's other statement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has finished defending ריש לקיש. Now it turns to the other half of the problem: רבי יוחנן still seems to contradict himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the chicken, רבי יוחנן said the holy item stays holy even after it runs away, because it is still in God's treasury. With the lost money, he said the owner is still responsible. Either the item is safe in God's treasury or the owner must replace it, so how can he hold both?

keyTerms.meaning: But (here: 'but still', pressing on what is left of the problem)
It is difficult; a contradiction

phrases.english: But that of Rabbi Yochanan
against that of Rabbi Yochanan is difficult!
phrases.notes: He means the runaway chicken ruling versus the lost money ruling from steps 20 and 22.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ריש לקיש's contradiction was solved in step 23, the גמרא returns to the second half of the double contradiction raised in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's two rulings: the runaway chicken and the lost בדק הבית money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'God's treasury' keeps the chicken holy wherever it goes, the same idea should free the owner from responsibility for lost money, yet רבי יוחנן makes him responsible.

steps.title: The difference between 'upon me' and 'this one is'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's rulings do not clash. The money case is where the person said 'עלי' (upon me). The chicken case is where he said 'הרי זו' (this one is).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן's statements also do not contradict each other. This one, about the lost money, is where he said 'upon me'. That one, about the chicken, is where he said 'this one is'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by showing that the two cases used different wording when the person made the item holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'עלי' puts a personal debt on the person, so he must keep paying until the money actually reaches the Temple. Saying 'הרי זו' makes only that specific item holy, so once it is holy it is in God's treasury wherever it ends up.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Upon me': a personal obligation the person takes on himself
'This one is': declaring a specific item holy
Also

steps.whatToRemember: 'עלי' means the person is obligated, so he is responsible if it is lost. 'הרי זו' means only the item is holy, so he is not responsible.

phrases.english: That of Rabbi Yochanan against that of Rabbi Yochanan
is also not difficult,
this is where he said 'upon me',
phrases.notes: This is the lost money case, where the owner stays responsible.

phrases.english: that is where he said 'this one is'.
phrases.notes: This is the chicken case, where it stays holy in God's treasury.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא) by the words used when the item was made holy.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases seemed to be the same kind of הקדש, so 'God's treasury' should apply to both.
steps.terutzMaskana: The money case involved 'עלי', a personal obligation. The chicken case involved 'הרי זו', where only the item is holy.

steps.title: So ריש לקיש frees him even when he said 'upon me'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a conclusion: since ריש לקיש disagreed with רבי יוחנן in the 'עלי' money case, he must hold there is no responsibility even when the person said 'עלי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: By implication, according to רבי שמעון בן לקיש, even though he said 'upon me', he is not responsible?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws out a surprising consequence of the last answer. This sets up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the money case was a case of 'עלי'. ריש לקיש said the owner is not responsible in that case. So ריש לקיש must hold that even a personal 'עלי' obligation goes away once the money is lost, and that sounds hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication; from this we can infer
Even though
Is held responsible / obligated

phrases.english: By implication, according to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
even though he said 'upon me',
he is not held responsible?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication about ריש לקיש from the answer given for רבי יוחנן in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling in the lost בדק הבית money case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that case was 'עלי', then ריש לקיש frees a person even from a personal obligation, and that seems wrong (the proof comes next).

steps.title: A ברייתא: with a נדר you are responsible
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that with a נדר ('עלי'), the person is responsible if the animal dies, is stolen, or is lost. That seems to contradict ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: Which is a נדר and which is a נדבה? A נדר is when someone says 'It is upon me to bring an עולה'. A נדבה is when someone says 'This animal is an עולה'. What is the difference between them? With a נדר, if it died, was stolen, or was lost, he is responsible for it. With a נדבה, if it died, was stolen, or was lost, he is not responsible for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that saying 'עלי' always makes a person responsible. That would contradict ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא clearly ties responsibility to the wording. 'עלי' (נדר) means he must replace a lost animal, while 'הרי זו' (נדבה) means he does not have to. So how can ריש לקיש say a person who said 'עלי' is not responsible?

keyTerms.meaning: A vow offering: 'It is upon me to bring...'
A gift offering: 'This animal is...'
A burnt offering
Responsibility to replace something if it is lost

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two up: נדר is the one with 'עלי' and carries responsibility. נדבה is 'הרי זו' and carries no responsibility.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
Which is a vow offering and which is a gift offering?
A vow offering: one who says 'It is upon me to bring a burnt offering',
A gift offering: one who says 'This is a burnt offering'.
And what is the difference between a vow and a gift offering?

phrases.aramaic: נֶדֶר – מֵתָה אוֹ נִגְנְבָה אוֹ שֶׁאָבְדָה,
phrases.english: A vow offering: if it died, or was stolen, or was lost,
he is responsible for it;

phrases.aramaic: נְדָבָה – מֵתָה אוֹ נִגְנְבָה אוֹ שֶׁאָבְדָה,
phrases.english: a gift offering: if it died, or was stolen, or was lost,
he is not responsible for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: אֵיזֶהוּ נֶדֶר וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא נְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source that turns the implication of step 26 into a real challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied position that ריש לקיש frees someone who said 'עלי'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא rules that 'עלי' (נדר) always brings responsibility for loss, so ריש לקיש cannot free such a person.

steps.title: The ברייתא is only about altar offerings
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the ברייתא speaks about קדשי מזבח, which still need to be offered. קדשי בדק הבית don't need offering, so even with 'עלי' there is no responsibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש would tell you: That rule applies only to items made holy for the altar, since they still need to be offered. But items made holy for Temple upkeep, which don't need to be offered, even though he said 'upon me', he is not responsible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by limiting the ברייתא to sacrifices brought on the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an altar offering, the promise is only complete once the animal is actually offered, so a lost animal leaves the promise unfinished. A בדק הבית gift doesn't need offering at all. Once it is set aside it already belongs to God's treasury, so even 'עלי' carries no further responsibility.

keyTerms.meaning: Items made holy to be offered on the altar
Items made holy for the upkeep of the Temple building
Still needs to be offered
These words apply (only to...)

steps.whatToRemember: In ריש לקיש's view, 'עלי' brings responsibility only for altar offerings, which still need to be offered. For בדק הבית there is no responsibility even with 'עלי'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the 'עלי' versus 'הרי זו' rule is not the whole story. It also matters what the item is for: the altar or Temple upkeep.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish could say to you:
These words apply to items holy for the altar,
since they still need to be offered,
but items holy for Temple upkeep,
which do not need to be offered,
even though he said 'upon me',
he is not held responsible.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הָנֵי מִילֵּי קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's challenge from step 27 by limiting its scope.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source: the ברייתא applies only to קדשי מזבח.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that 'עלי' always brings responsibility, for any kind of הקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Responsibility from 'עלי' applies only to altar offerings that still need to be offered. For בדק הבית, ריש לקיש holds there is no responsibility.

steps.title: A משנה seems to make 'עלי' binding even for בדק הבית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: 'this ox is an עולה' or 'this house is a קרבן' means no responsibility if they are destroyed, but adding 'עלי' makes the person pay. This seems to go against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: If someone says 'This ox is an עולה' or 'This house is a קרבן', and the ox died or the house collapsed, he is not responsible for them. But if he says 'This ox is upon me as an עולה' or 'This house is upon me as a קרבן', and the ox died or the house collapsed, he must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's answer from Step 28 with a משנה. In that משנה, even a house, which goes to בדק הבית, creates responsibility when the person said 'עלי'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש just said that for קדשי בדק הבית there is no responsibility, even with 'עלי'. A house can't be brought on the altar, so 'this house is a קרבן' must mean a gift for בדק הבית. Yet the משנה says that with 'עלי' he must pay, which looks like a direct contradiction to ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Responsibility: having to replace or pay for the item if something happens to it
A burnt offering, burned completely on the altar
Here: a gift to the Temple. For a house it means a gift for upkeep (בדק הבית)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the house is being sacrificed. A house can't go on the altar, so 'קרבן' here means a donation to the Temple treasury for בדק הבית. That is exactly why it challenges ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: One who says 'This ox is a burnt offering,'
phrases.notes: This משנה is in ערכין 20b.

phrases.english: or 'This house is an offering' –
phrases.notes: A house can't go on the altar, so this means a gift for the Temple's upkeep.

phrases.english: and the ox died, or the house collapsed –
he is not responsible for them;
'This ox is upon me as a burnt offering,'
or 'This house is upon me as an offering' –
and the ox died or the house collapsed –
he must pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's answer in Step 28 that 'עלי' creates no responsibility for בדק הבית.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's position that even with 'עלי' there is no responsibility for קדשי בדק הבית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's house case is בדק הבית, yet saying 'עלי' makes the person pay, which is the opposite of what ריש לקיש says.

steps.title: Paying applies only when the item is gone; if it still exists, it is in God's treasury
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's payment applies only when the ox died or the house fell, since they no longer exist. For בדק הבית, an item that still exists (lost or stolen) is already in God's treasury, because 'the earth is the Lord's'. As תוספות notes, the ox side is not precise: an altar ox obligates him even when lost or stolen.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only where the ox died and the house collapsed. Then he must pay, because they no longer exist. But where they still exist, wherever it is, it is in the treasury of the Merciful One, as it is written: 'The earth is the Lord's and all that fills it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by limiting the משנה: paying is required only when the item is completely destroyed. When a בדק הבית item still exists somewhere, the person owes nothing. תוספות qualifies the ox side: an altar ox remains his responsibility even when lost or stolen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of loss: destroyed (died, collapsed) and still existing somewhere (lost, stolen). For בדק הבית, an item that still exists is counted as already in the Temple's possession, since the whole world belongs to God. So ריש לקיש's case of lost or stolen items fits his ruling, and the משנה only speaks about total destruction.

keyTerms.meaning: This applies only... A phrase that narrows a rule to a specific case
They don't exist / they do exist
The treasury of the Merciful One (God's treasury)
The earth and all that fills it belong to God

steps.whatToRemember: For בדק הבית: if the item was destroyed and he said 'עלי', he pays. If it was only lost or stolen, it still exists 'in God's treasury', so even with 'עלי' he does not pay (according to ריש לקיש).
steps.whyThisMatters: This creates a clear split between destroyed items and items that still exist somewhere. That split lets ריש לקיש's view stand next to the משנה.

phrases.english: These words apply where the ox died
and the house collapsed; he must pay
because they no longer exist.
But where they still exist,
phrases.notes: This means a case like lost or stolen. The item is gone from him, but it still exists somewhere.

phrases.english: wherever it is,
it is in the treasury of the Merciful One,
as it is written: 'The earth is the Lord's and all that fills it.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 24:1

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּמֵת הַשּׁוֹר וְנָפַל הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 29 by limiting the משנה to items that were destroyed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: for בדק הבית the משנה speaks only of destroyed items, not lost or stolen ones (the altar-ox side is not precise - an altar ox obligates even when lost or stolen).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה makes 'עלי' create full responsibility for בדק הבית in every case, against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: For בדק הבית, responsibility applies only when the item no longer exists; a lost or stolen item is still in God's treasury. This does not release an altar ox: even lost or stolen, it remains his responsibility.

steps.title: רב המנונא: in ערכין no one is responsible, even with 'עלי'
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא says both sides agree that someone who pledges ערכין is not responsible, even though he said 'עלי', because a pledge of ערכין cannot be said without 'עלי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: Everyone agrees about ערכין that even though he said 'upon me', he is not responsible. What is the reason? Because it cannot be said by him without 'upon me'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא brings a new rule: in a pledge of ערכין, both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree there is no responsibility, even with 'עלי'. He explains that the word 'עלי' is simply the only way to say this kind of pledge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually 'עלי' shows the person took extra responsibility on himself. But in ערכין he has no other wording available, so 'עלי' does not show any extra commitment. That is why even רבי יוחנן, who usually holds 'עלי' makes a person responsible, agrees here.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees: both sides of a dispute accept this point
Pledges to give a person's fixed 'value' set by the Torah to the Temple
What is the reason?

steps.whatToRemember: 'עלי' creates responsibility only when the person could have said it another way. In ערכין there is no other way, so 'עלי' adds nothing.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:
Everyone agrees about valuations,
that even though he said 'upon me' –
he is not responsible.
What is the reason?
Because it cannot be said by him without 'upon me'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים בַּעֲרָכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a point that both sides of the רבי יוחנן–ריש לקיש dispute agree on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ערכין, saying 'עלי' does not create responsibility, because there is no way to pledge ערכין without it.

steps.title: Showing that ערכין can't be pledged without 'עלי'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows why 'עלי' is needed: if he says only 'my value' or 'so-and-so's value', it is unclear who has to pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: How else should he say it? Should he say 'My value'? Upon whom is it? Should he say 'So-and-so's value'? Upon whom is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב המנונא's reason by trying other ways to word the pledge. Each one fails because it doesn't say who must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an ox or a house, you can point to an existing object and say 'this is holy' without 'עלי'. A value is not an object, so without 'עלי' there is no one obligated to pay. That proves 'עלי' in ערכין is just the basic wording, not an extra promise.

keyTerms.meaning: How should he say it?
My value (my ערך)
The value of so-and-so
Upon whom? Who is obligated?

phrases.english: How should he say it?
Should he say 'My value'? Upon whom?
Should he say 'So-and-so's value'? Upon whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the reason given in Step 31 by showing that no other wording works.
steps.raayaObject: רב המנונא's reason that ערכין cannot be pledged without 'עלי'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logical test: the other wordings ('my value', 'so-and-so's value') don't say who must pay.

steps.title: רבא: A person could pledge ערכין using 'הריני'
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב המנונא's reason. A person does not need to say 'עלי' to pledge ערכין. He could say 'הריני בערכי' or 'הריני בערך פלוני'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: Let him say 'I am obligated for my value' or 'I am obligated for so-and-so's value'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the reason רב המנונא gave in Step 31. That reason was that ערכין can't be said without 'עלי'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא explained that the word 'עלי' in ערכין doesn't add responsibility, because it is always needed to show who pays. רבא answers that 'הריני' already shows who pays. So 'עלי' is not the only way to say it, and the reason falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it, an objection against a statement
'Here I am', a phrase that makes the speaker obligated
My value, the fixed amount the תורה sets for a person
So-and-so, an unnamed person

phrases.english: Rava objected to it:
Let him say, "I am [obligated] with my value,"
"I am [obligated] with so-and-so's value"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of Steps 31-32, which said 'עלי' is required in ערכין.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's claim that a pledge of ערכין cannot be made without 'עלי'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is another way to word the pledge, 'הריני', so 'עלי' is not required. That means 'עלי' should carry its normal meaning of responsibility.

steps.title: A second challenge begins: רבי נתן's ברייתא on the פסוק of ערכין
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds another challenge by quoting a ברייתא. רבי נתן asks why the פסוק says 'and he shall give your valuation… holy to ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, it was taught: רבי נתן says, 'And he shall give your valuation on that day, holy to ה׳.' Why does the פסוק need to say this?
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up a second objection against רב המנונא. The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא, and the challenge itself comes once the ברייתא is fully quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ועוד' tells us a second, separate challenge is coming. רבי נתן notices extra wording in the פסוק about ערכין and asks what it comes to teach. His answer, which starts in the next step, will be the basis of the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, which brings in an additional challenge
What does the פסוק come to teach? Asked when wording seems extra
Holy to ה׳

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught: Rabbi Natan says:
"And he shall give your valuation
on that day, holy to ה׳"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:23

phrases.english: What does the verse come to teach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge after רבא's first objection in Step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's statement that one who pledges ערכין is not responsible
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about the ערכין פסוק is brought. Its full point, which continues on the next amud, will be used against רב המנונא.

steps.title: רבי נתן begins his answer: redeemed הקדש and מעשר carry no responsibility
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן starts explaining the פסוק. He recalls that הקדש and מעשר can be redeemed onto ordinary coins, and if those coins are stolen or lost, the owners are not responsible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we have found that consecrated items and tithes, which are redeemed onto ordinary money, if the money was stolen or lost, the owners are not responsible for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן begins answering his own question by first stating a rule about הקדש and מעשר. This is background, and his point about ערכין continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When הקדש or מעשר is redeemed, its holiness moves onto the coins. If those coins then go missing, the owner owes nothing. By starting with this known rule, רבי נתן is preparing a contrast with ערכין, which the פסוק will treat differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Items given to the בית המקדש
Tithes, here especially מעשר שני, which can be redeemed
Are redeemed, meaning their holiness is moved onto money
Responsibility to replace something if it is lost

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT yet רבי נתן's conclusion about ערכין. It is only the background rule. The ערכין part that contrasts with it comes next.

phrases.english: Because we have found regarding consecrated items and tithes
that they are redeemed onto ordinary money,
if [the coins] were stolen or lost,
they are not responsible for them,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the ברייתא's answer to the question asked in Step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Partial answer. It sets out the background rule that redeemed הקדש and מעשר carry no responsibility if lost, as a lead-in to the ערכין contrast.
